note: Commonly reported problems. Not every vehicle will have them.

aeb.s: The vehicle brakes hard by itself with nothing ahead, or collision warnings go off for no reason.
aeb.w: Keep the windshield camera and radar clean. Get software updates and check for recalls.

hv_contactor.s: Sudden loss of drive power, a 'service vehicle' or hybrid warning, or the car won't go into Ready.
hv_contactor.w: Get it to a dealer. High-voltage parts are not a DIY job.

ev_fire_recall.s: Usually no warning. Some packs can overheat; the recall may limit charging until it's fixed.
ev_fire_recall.w: Follow the recall instructions (some say park outside and charge to 80% or less) and get the free repair.

coolant_intrusion.s: Losing coolant with no leak, white smoke, misfire at startup, overheating.
coolant_intrusion.w: Ford covers many under recall or extended warranty; check your VIN. Don't keep driving while coolant drops.

fire_recall.s: Often no warning. Some have a fuel or oil smell under the hood or a leak.
fire_recall.w: Get the free recall repair soon. If the recall says park outside, do that until it's fixed.

airbag_recall.s: Airbag warning light on the dash, or a passenger airbag 'off' light that shouldn't be.
airbag_recall.w: Have the airbag system scanned and check for recalls. An airbag light means the airbags may not work in a crash.

rollaway_recall.s: The vehicle can roll after you think it's in Park, or the shifter doesn't respond right.
rollaway_recall.w: Always set the parking brake and check the dash says P. Get the recall or software fix.

pedal_recall.s: The gas pedal sticks down or comes back up slowly.
pedal_recall.w: If it sticks: shift to Neutral, brake, and pull over. Get the free recall fix.

hub_bolt_recall.s: A clunk or wobble from a wheel; in bad cases the wheel can come loose.
hub_bolt_recall.w: Get the free recall repair. Don't ignore a new clunk from a wheel.

axle_recall.s: A clunk from the rear, then loss of drive. The vehicle can roll in Park if the axle bolt breaks.
axle_recall.w: Get the free recall repair and use the parking brake until then.

frame_recall.s: Flaking, soft or holed frame rails, especially near the rear springs and control arms.
frame_recall.w: Have the frame inspected. Toyota replaced frames or bought back many trucks; ask a dealer about your VIN.

ev_ice_recall.s: Knocking, rough running, stalling, or the engine won't start.
ev_ice_recall.w: Check your VIN for the engine recall. Stop driving if the engine knocks.

l87_recall.s: Knocking from the engine, low oil pressure, or the engine shutting off while driving.
l87_recall.w: Check your VIN for the 6.2L (L87) recall. Stop driving if it knocks.

theta2.s: A knock that gets faster with engine speed, oil light, stalling, or a check engine light. In bad cases the engine seizes.
theta2.w: Hyundai/Kia recalled many and added a lifetime engine warranty on some. Check your VIN; stop driving if it knocks.

trim_recall.s: A loose trim panel or a taillight that stops working.

early_build.s: No single symptom. The first year of a new model often has several recalls and software updates.
early_build.w: Look up your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls and ask a dealer to do any open recalls and updates.

brake_actuator.s: Brake and ABS warning lights, a buzzing pump noise, a harder or different-feeling pedal.
brake_actuator.w: Get it checked right away. The brake actuator or pump is replaced; some are covered by extended warranty.

iccu.s: A 12V battery warning, loss of power while driving, or the car stops charging.
iccu.w: Get it to a dealer; the charging unit (ICCU) is replaced under recall or warranty.

hybrid_battery.s: Worse gas mileage, the engine runs more often, a hybrid system warning, less electric range.
hybrid_battery.w: Get the hybrid battery tested. Rebuilt and new packs are available; many carry an 8 to 10 year warranty.

hybrid.s: A hybrid or 'check EV system' warning, loss of power, won't go into Ready, charging stops or is slow.
hybrid.w: Get it to a dealer or a hybrid/EV specialist. Check warranties; high-voltage parts are often covered for years.

tdi_fix.s: No symptom. The emissions fix (software and parts) was done under the settlement; some notice lower mileage.
tdi_fix.w: Check that the emissions fix was done; it's needed for registration in some states.

ps60.s: Losing coolant, white smoke, coolant tank pressurizing, oil and coolant temps far apart.
ps60.w: Find a diesel shop that knows the 6.0. Head studs, EGR cooler and oil cooler fixes are well known.

ficm.s: Hard start or no start in cold weather, rough running until warm, misfire.
ficm.w: Test FICM voltage (about 48 volts). The module is repaired or replaced.

diesel_crank.s: A deep knock, metal in the oil, or the engine suddenly quits.
diesel_crank.w: Stop driving it. Check for recalls and warranty extensions; a failed crankshaft usually means a new engine.

diesel_emissions.s: DEF or exhaust warning lights, reduced power (limp mode), a countdown to a speed limit, frequent regenerations.
diesel_emissions.w: A diesel shop scans the codes. Sensors and DEF heaters are common; drive on the highway to let the filter clean itself.

secondary_air.s: Check engine light (P0410, P0411, P0491), a loud whirring for a minute after a cold start.
secondary_air.w: The air pump or check valve is replaced. Usually safe to drive; it only runs right after a cold start.

diesel_fuel.s: Hard starting, loss of power, stalling, or a sudden no-start. Metal from a failed pump can ruin the whole fuel system.
diesel_fuel.w: Use clean fuel and change fuel filters on time. If the pump fails, the whole system must be cleaned or replaced.

carbon.s: Rough idle, misfire on cold starts, slowly losing power and gas mileage.
carbon.w: Direct-injection engines need the intake valves cleaned (walnut blasting) every 60,000 to 100,000 miles.

intercooler.s: Misfire or stumble when you floor it, mostly in humid or rainy weather.
intercooler.w: Ford installed a deflector on the intercooler. Ask a dealer about the fix.

turbo_rattle.s: A metallic rattle from the turbo at idle or when letting off the gas.
turbo_rattle.w: The wastegate linkage wears. Usually not urgent; replace if it sets a boost code.

turbo.s: Loss of power, a whistle or siren sound, blue or white smoke, a check engine light (P0299).
turbo.w: Check for oil leaks at the turbo lines and boost leaks. Change oil on time; turbos die from old oil.

iwe.s: Grinding from the front wheels in 2WD, or 4x4 slow to engage.
iwe.w: Usually a cracked vacuum line or check valve; cheap to fix. The hubs (IWE) can also be replaced.

ptu.s: A burning gear-oil smell, leaks between the engine and transmission, grinding or a clunk when turning.
ptu.w: Change the PTU fluid often (it's often never changed). Replace the seals or the unit before it fails.

transfer_case_pump.s: Transfer case fluid leaking, a hole worn in the case, whining from the middle of the truck.
transfer_case_pump.w: A pump rub kit fixes it if caught before the case wears through.

fourwd.s: 4WD won't engage or disengage, a 'Service 4WD' light, grinding or binding when turning.
fourwd.w: The shift motor (encoder) or actuator is a common, moderate fix. Check the transfer case fluid.

dct.s: Shudder or jerky starts from a stop, hesitation, rolling back on hills, slipping in stop-and-go traffic, a transmission warning.
dct.w: Ask a dealer for software updates and clutch or control unit fixes; some had extended warranties. Avoid creeping in traffic.

strawberry_milkshake.s: Pink, milky transmission fluid or coolant, slipping, shuddering, or overheating.
strawberry_milkshake.w: Stop driving and check both fluids. The radiator's built-in transmission cooler cracked; replace the radiator and flush early.

cvt.s: Judder or shudder when pulling away, a whine that rises with speed, RPM flaring without speeding up, or limp mode.
cvt.w: Ask a dealer about software updates and extended CVT warranties for your VIN. Change the CVT fluid on schedule.

tc_shudder.s: A shake like driving over rumble strips at 25 to 50 mph on light gas.
tc_shudder.w: A fluid exchange with the updated fluid often fixes it; if not, the torque converter is replaced.

conductor_plate.s: Sudden harsh shifts, stuck in one gear (limp mode), or the speedometer drops to zero.
conductor_plate.w: The circuit board inside the transmission is replaced; no full rebuild needed.

wave_plate.s: Loses 3rd, 5th and reverse gears, or goes into limp mode.
wave_plate.w: A transmission shop replaces the 3-5-R wave plate. Common on GM 6-speeds.

shift_to_park.s: A 'Shift to Park' message that won't clear, so the vehicle won't shut off and the battery can drain.
shift_to_park.w: The shifter's park switch wears out. A cheap shifter part fixes it; GM has special coverage on many.

tcm.s: Erratic shifting, stuck in one gear, a transmission warning light.
tcm.w: The module that controls shifting is scanned, reprogrammed or replaced.

ecm.s: Stalling, hesitation, no start, or a check engine light with no clear cause.
ecm.w: A shop checks for software updates or recalls on the engine computer.

manual_notchy.s: Hard or notchy shifts, gears grinding, especially when cold or shifting fast.
manual_notchy.w: Fresh gear oil and a shifter bushing kit help. Grinding into gear can mean worn synchros inside.

clutch_hydraulic.s: Clutch pedal goes soft, sticks to the floor, or it's hard to shift into gear.
clutch_hydraulic.w: Check the clutch fluid. The slave or master cylinder is replaced and the system bled.

ac_compressor.s: A/C blows warm, the compressor clicks on and off or makes noise.
ac_compressor.w: A shop checks pressures and the compressor clutch. Fix leaks first so the new part lasts.

ac_leak.s: A/C blows warm, then cold after a recharge, then warm again.
ac_leak.w: Have the leak found (dye test) before paying for another recharge.

fan_clutch.s: Running hot at idle or in traffic, or a loud roaring fan.
fan_clutch.w: The engine fan clutch locks up or slips. A common, moderate repair.

clutch_wear.s: Engine revs up but the vehicle doesn't speed up (slipping), a burnt smell, the clutch grabs high.
clutch_wear.w: A worn clutch is replaced with the flywheel checked or resurfaced. Don't ride the pedal.

harsh_shift.s: Harsh, clunky or late shifts, jerks at low speed, hunting between gears, a delay before it moves.
harsh_shift.w: Ask a dealer for software updates and a transmission relearn. Check the fluid level and condition.

trans_failure.s: Slipping, revs flaring between gears, delay going into drive or reverse, burnt-smelling fluid, losing gears.
trans_failure.w: Check the fluid level and smell. A transmission shop scans for codes; catching it early can mean a smaller repair than a rebuild.

afm_oil.s: Needing to add a quart of oil between changes, fouled spark plugs, blue smoke at startup.
afm_oil.w: Check the oil every fill-up. Shops can replace the oil deflector/PCV parts or piston rings in bad cases.

lifter.s: A ticking that gets louder, misfire codes, rough running, a check engine light.
lifter.w: Get it checked soon. A collapsed lifter can wreck the camshaft. Many owners disable cylinder shutoff after the repair.

vcm_vibration.s: A vibration or drone at steady cruising when half the cylinders shut off.
vcm_vibration.w: Worn engine mounts make it worse. New mounts or a software update help.

vcm_misfire.s: Misfire codes, rough running, fouled spark plugs (often on the rear cylinders).
vcm_misfire.w: New plugs fix it short-term. Ask about software updates and piston ring fixes.

vtc_rattle.s: A loud grinding rattle for a second or two right after a cold start.
vtc_rattle.w: The cam phaser (VTC actuator) is replaced. Keep the oil full and fresh.

vvti_line.s: Sudden big oil leak or oil spraying from the engine, oil light on.
vvti_line.w: Stop driving if the oil light comes on. The rubber oil line was replaced with an all-metal one; check for the warranty fix.

timing_belt.s: Usually no warning. If it breaks, the engine stops and cranks but won't start, and on many engines the valves get bent.
timing_belt.w: Replace it on schedule (often 60,000 to 105,000 miles; check your manual) with the water pump. If you don't know when it was done, do it.

timing_chain.s: Rattle at startup, a check engine light with P0008, P0016 or P0017, rough running.
timing_chain.w: Don't wait: a jumped chain can wreck the engine. It's a big job. Changing oil on time is the best prevention.

valve_tick.s: A light ticking that follows engine speed, sometimes a rough idle.
valve_tick.w: A valve clearance adjustment on the maintenance schedule. Cheap if done before damage.

injector_tick.s: A loud ticking from the top of the engine.
injector_tick.w: Direct-injection injectors tick normally. Have it checked if the sound changes or comes with a misfire.

valve_failure.s: A misfire on one cylinder, rough running, loss of power. Can lead to serious engine damage.
valve_failure.w: Get a compression or leak-down test. Check your VIN for recalls.

knock_sensor.s: Check engine light with codes P0327 or P0332. Usually runs fine.
knock_sensor.w: The sensors sit under the intake, so it's mostly labor. Replace the sensors and wiring together.

ims.s: Metal flakes in the oil filter, a rattle, then sudden engine failure.
ims.w: An upgraded IMS bearing is installed before it fails, often during a clutch job.

rotary.s: Hard starts when hot, low power, burning oil, or flooding after short trips.
rotary.w: Get a rotary compression test. Let it warm up fully before shutting off, and keep the oil topped up.

wheel_bearing.s: A hum that gets louder with speed and changes when you curve, ABS light sometimes.
wheel_bearing.w: Replace the bearing/hub. Lifts and big tires wear them faster.

knock.s: A deep knock that gets faster with engine speed, an oil light, or metal in the oil.
knock.w: Stop driving if it knocks. Check the oil level and your VIN for recalls or engine warranty extensions.

balance_shaft.s: Check engine light with cam/crank timing codes (P0016, P0017), rough running.
balance_shaft.w: The balance shaft gear wears; it's a big repair. Check for warranty extensions.

harmonic_balancer.s: A wobbling pulley at the front of the engine, belt squeal, the belt walking off.
harmonic_balancer.w: Replace the balancer before it comes apart and takes the belt with it.

oil_gallery.s: Oil pressure drops at hot idle, the oil light flickers, ticking.
oil_gallery.w: The oil gallery gasket inside the engine is replaced. Watch the oil pressure gauge.

oil_dilution.s: The oil level goes UP and smells like gas, mostly in cold weather and short trips.
oil_dilution.w: Get the software update or warranty fix. Change oil more often in winter and take longer drives.

sludge.s: Oil light flickering, ticking, burning oil, thick black gunk under the oil cap.
sludge.w: Change oil on time with the right oil. Caught early, a cleaning and new oil pickup help; bad cases need an engine.

oil_consumption.s: Oil runs low between changes with no drips, blue smoke at startup, the oil light comes on.
oil_consumption.w: Check oil every fill-up and keep it full. Ask about warranty extensions; piston rings or seals are the fix.

oil_cooler.s: Oil (sometimes coolant too) leaking at the top or back of the engine, burning oil smell.
oil_cooler.w: The housing and gasket are replaced. Common and well known, so get a quote from a shop that's done it.

head_gasket.s: Losing coolant, white smoke that smells sweet, overheating, oil or coolant leaking at the side of the engine.
head_gasket.w: Fix it early. Left alone, it overheats the engine. A shop can test for exhaust gas in the coolant.

oil_leak.s: Brown or black drips under the engine, a burning oil smell, the oil level dropping.
oil_leak.w: Clean the engine and find the source. A valve cover gasket is cheap; a rear main seal is a big job. Keep the oil topped up.

internal_wp.s: Coolant goes low with no leak, milky oil, overheating. The pump is inside the engine, so a leak goes into the oil.
internal_wp.w: Stop driving if the oil looks milky. A big job (the timing chain comes off); many replace it early, around 100,000 miles.

electric_wp.s: Overheating warning, temperature climbing, fan on high, reduced power mode.
electric_wp.w: The electric pump fails without warning. Replace it, often with the thermostat.

water_pump.s: Coolant drips at the front of the engine, sweet smell, low coolant warning, a whine or grinding from the belt area.
water_pump.w: Replace the pump (and thermostat if it's nearby) before it overheats the engine. If the timing belt drives it, do both.

intake_coolant.s: Losing coolant with no puddle, sweet smell, overheating, milky oil in bad cases.
intake_coolant.w: Fix it early. Left alone, coolant mixes with oil and ruins the engine bearings.

coolant_sensor.s: Temp gauge reads wrong or jumps, fans run all the time, hard starting, worse gas mileage.
coolant_sensor.w: A cheap sensor. A shop checks its reading against the real engine temperature.

coolant_leak.s: Low coolant warning, sweet smell, drips under the front, temperature rising.
coolant_leak.w: Find the leak (hoses, radiator, reservoir, housings) before it overheats. Never open a hot radiator cap.

pcv.s: Whistling or squealing at idle, oil leaks, rough idle, lean codes.
pcv.w: The PCV valve or valve cover is replaced. Cheap compared to the oil leaks it causes.

intake_leak.s: Rough or high idle, hissing, lean codes (P0171/P0174).
intake_leak.w: A shop smoke-tests the intake to find the leak.

throttle_body.s: Stalling, idle too high or low, a wrench light or reduced power mode, gas pedal that doesn't respond.
throttle_body.w: Clean the throttle body first. If it keeps happening, it's replaced; check for warranty coverage.

injector.s: Rough running, smoke, a fuel smell, or (on diesels) the oil level rising.
injector.w: The injectors are tested and replaced, often as a set.

tipm.s: Random electrical problems: horn or wipers turning on alone, no start, fuel pump won't run, lights acting up.
tipm.w: The fuse/relay box (TIPM) is repaired or replaced. Check for recalls and extended coverage.

fuel_pump.s: Long crank before starting, sputtering under load, or cranks but won't start.
fuel_pump.w: Test fuel pressure. The pump is in the tank; check recalls first, since many were recalled.

fuel_sender.s: Gauges stick, jump or drop to zero; the fuel gauge reads wrong.
fuel_sender.w: The gauge motors or the fuel level sender (in the tank) are replaced. A cluster repair service is cheaper than a new cluster.

evap_fill.s: The gas pump keeps clicking off, a fuel smell, hard starting right after filling up, a check engine light (EVAP).
evap_fill.w: The EVAP vent or purge valve is replaced. Usually cheap.

coil.s: Shaking at idle, a flashing check engine light, a misfire code (P0301 to P0308).
coil.w: Swap the suspect coil to another cylinder; if the misfire moves, replace it. Change spark plugs at the same time.

plug_blowout.s: A sudden loud ticking or popping from the engine with a misfire. The spark plug can shoot out of the head.
plug_blowout.w: Stop and tow it. The threads in the head are repaired with an insert.

plug_break.s: No symptom while driving. The plugs break off in the head when a shop removes them, raising the tune-up cost.
plug_break.w: Use a shop that knows the special tool and steps (warm engine, soak, slow turns). Ask for a quote first.

plug_foul.w: Replace the spark plugs and find out why they fouled (oil or fuel).

distributor.s: Stalling or no start when hot, misfire, the tachometer drops to zero.
distributor.w: The distributor or igniter is replaced. Common on older Toyotas and GMs.

crank_sensor.s: Stalling when hot, then it restarts after cooling down; or cranks but won't start.
crank_sensor.w: A cheap sensor. A scan tool usually shows the code; check for recalls.

cat_theft.s: A sudden, very loud roar from under the vehicle after it was parked.
cat_theft.w: Look underneath, then file a police report and an insurance claim. A shield or cage helps prevent it.

cat_engine.s: Check engine light (P0420), a rattle, burning oil, or a loss of power. Broken converter pieces can get pulled into the engine.
cat_engine.w: Get it checked soon; replacing the converter early can save the engine. Check for warranty extensions.

cat.s: Check engine light (P0420), a rotten egg smell, a rattle under the vehicle, or low power.
cat.w: Fix any misfire first (it kills converters). A loose heat shield rattle is a cheap clamp fix.

exhaust_fumes.s: Exhaust smell inside, headaches or drowsiness, mostly when accelerating hard.
exhaust_fumes.w: Get it checked now; carbon monoxide is dangerous. Ford has service fixes for the rear body seals.

exhaust.s: A ticking or puffing sound, loudest when cold, an exhaust smell.
exhaust.w: A shop replaces the manifold, studs or gasket. Not urgent unless it's loud or you smell exhaust inside.

passlock.s: Security light on; cranks but won't start, or starts then dies.
passlock.w: Try the 10-minute relearn (key on, wait until the security light stops flashing). The fix is often the ignition switch wiring.

ignition_switch_recall.s: The engine shuts off while driving; power steering and airbags can turn off.
ignition_switch_recall.w: Serious recall. Keep only the key on the ring until it's fixed.

steering_lock.s: The key won't turn or the car says 'key not detected' / won't start; the steering wheel stays locked.
steering_lock.w: The electronic steering lock is replaced. Some had recalls or service fixes.

ignition.s: The key is hard to turn or sticks, or the car won't start with the key.
ignition.w: The lock cylinder or switch is replaced. Don't hang a heavy key ring from the key.

starter.s: One loud click or nothing when you turn the key, while the lights stay bright.
starter.w: Test the battery first. The starter is replaced.

stop_start.s: The engine doesn't restart smoothly after an auto stop, stop-start quits working, battery warnings.
stop_start.w: Stop-start needs a healthy (often AGM) battery. Test or replace it, and ask for software updates.

battery_drain.s: Dead battery after sitting a day or two, battery warnings, a new battery that dies early.
battery_drain.w: Get the battery tested and a parasitic draw test (something staying on). Software updates fix many.

infotainment.s: The touchscreen freezes, reboots, goes black or touches itself; Bluetooth, CarPlay or the backup camera drop out.
infotainment.w: Restart the system (hold power), then ask a dealer for software updates. Screens are replaced under warranty or recall on some.

eps.s: Steering suddenly gets heavy, a power steering warning light.
eps.w: Check for recalls first; many electric steering motors were recalled. Have the codes scanned.

electrical.s: Random warning lights, things that work sometimes and not others, a dead battery.
electrical.w: A shop checks grounds, connectors and modules for codes. Look for water leaks near the modules.

blower.s: Fan only works on some speeds or not at all.
blower.w: The blower motor resistor or motor is replaced. Usually an easy fix.

blend_door.s: Clicking or tapping behind the dash, air stuck hot or cold, or different temperatures on each side.
blend_door.w: The small door motor (actuator) behind the dash is replaced. An inexpensive part; labor depends on the spot.

brake_vacuum_pump.s: Hard brake pedal that takes much more effort to stop, sometimes an oil leak at the pump.
brake_vacuum_pump.w: Get it checked now; the brakes still work but need a lot more force.

brake_line.s: Soft or sinking brake pedal, brake fluid on the frame rail or near a wheel.
brake_line.w: Don't drive it. Rusted lines are replaced as a whole line, not just the leak.

caliper.s: Pulls to one side, one wheel hot or smelling burnt, uneven pad wear.
caliper.w: Replace the caliper and slide pins. Clean and grease them at every brake job.

brake_vibration.s: Shaking steering wheel or pulsing pedal when braking.
brake_vibration.w: Replace or resurface the rotors and torque the wheels right.

brake_feel.s: The brake pedal feels soft, grabby or different from stop to stop.
brake_feel.w: Have the brakes and brake fluid checked, and ask about software updates (hybrids).

brake_wear.s: Squealing or grinding when braking, pads wearing out early.
brake_wear.w: Check pad thickness at every tire rotation. Quality pads and rotors last longer.

death_wobble.s: Violent shaking of the steering wheel and front end after hitting a bump at 40 to 60 mph. Only slowing way down stops it.
death_wobble.w: Have the track bar, ball joints, tie rods and steering damper checked. A new damper alone just hides it.

air_susp.s: Sagging overnight, the compressor running a lot, a suspension warning, a bouncy or harsh ride.
air_susp.w: Air springs and compressors wear out. Replace the leaking spring and the relay. Coil spring conversions are an option.

ball_joint.s: Clunk over bumps, loose steering, uneven tire wear. A broken ball joint can make a wheel fold under.
ball_joint.w: Get it checked soon and check recalls. Replace both sides and get an alignment.

steering_shaft.s: A clunk or knock felt in the steering wheel when turning slowly or parked.
steering_shaft.w: The intermediate steering shaft is greased or replaced. A common, cheap fix.

ps.s: Whining when turning, stiff steering, power steering fluid leaks.
ps.w: Fix leaks early so the pump doesn't run dry. Use the right fluid.

camber_wear.s: Tires wearing on the inside edge.
camber_wear.w: Get an alignment; some need camber kits. Rotate the tires often.

spring.s: Sagging corner, clunk over bumps, the vehicle leans or sits low.
spring.w: Broken springs are replaced in pairs.

hood_latch.s: The hood is hard to close or open, or won't latch right.
hood_latch.w: Clean and grease the latch; check for the recall. A bad latch can let the hood fly up.

frame_rust.s: Bubbling paint, rust holes in the rocker panels, cab corners, wheel arches or frame.
frame_rust.w: Wash the underside in winter and treat rust early. Have the frame checked before buying one used.

suspension.s: Clunks or creaks over bumps, loose or wandering steering, uneven tire wear.
suspension.w: A shop checks bushings, control arms and tie rods. Cheap parts; get an alignment after.

motor_mount.s: Vibration at idle, a clunk when shifting or pulling away, the engine rocks.
motor_mount.w: Replace the worn mounts. Cheap parts on most vehicles.

differential.s: A whine or howl at speed that changes on and off the gas, groaning on turns, gear oil leaking at the axle.
differential.w: Check and change the differential fluid (with friction modifier if it has a limited slip). Fix leaking seals.

window.s: Window drops, goes up crooked, moves slowly, or you hear grinding or clicking in the door.
window.w: The window regulator (or motor) is replaced. An easy DIY on many vehicles.

liftgate_strut.s: The liftgate or hatch won't stay up.
liftgate_strut.w: Replace the gas struts. An easy DIY; prop the hatch safely while you work.

glass_hinge.s: The rear window hinge cracks, the rear glass won't stay up, or the rear wiper stops.
glass_hinge.w: The hinges are replaced; some had extended coverage.

door.s: Doors won't lock or unlock with the button, a buzzing in the door, a door won't open, or the sliding door gets stuck.
door.w: The lock actuator, latch or sliding door cable is replaced. Check for recalls on door latches.

interior.s: Worn seats or trim, a sagging headliner, rattles.
interior.w: Cosmetic. An upholstery or trim shop can fix most of it.

water_leak.s: Wet carpet or seats after rain or a car wash, water dripping from the headliner, a musty smell, foggy windows.
water_leak.w: Clear the sunroof drains (compressed air or a trimmer line) and check the door and window seals.

dashboard.s: The dashboard cracks, bubbles, or gets sticky and shiny in the heat.
dashboard.w: Cosmetic. A dash cover helps. Some makers (like Toyota/Lexus) replaced dashboards under warranty extensions.

paint.s: Paint or clear coat peeling or chipping, faded plastic trim.
paint.w: Cosmetic. Keep it waxed and ask a dealer if there's a paint warranty extension.

windshield.s: Cracks that start at the edge of the windshield without a rock hit.
windshield.w: Insurance glass coverage often pays. Use original-quality glass so the cameras work.

wheels.s: A slow air leak or vibration from a cracked alloy wheel.
wheels.w: Check the inside of the wheel for cracks; replace a cracked wheel. Don't weld it.

headlight.s: Headlights flicker, go out, or fog up inside.
headlight.w: Check the bulb, ballast and seals. Foggy lenses can be resealed or replaced.

wiper.s: Wipers stop, move slowly, or park in the wrong spot.
wiper.w: The wiper motor or linkage is replaced.

heat_cabin.s: The floor or center console gets hot on long drives.
heat_cabin.w: Ask a dealer about added heat shielding.

generic_recall.w: Look up your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls and get any open recalls done.

generic_engine.s: A check engine light, rough running or loss of power.
generic_engine.w: A shop scans the codes and checks for recalls and service bulletins.

gm_ls_v8.s: A ticking or puffing sound when the engine is cold that fades as it warms up.
gm_ls_v8.w: A shop drills out the broken bolts and replaces the gasket. Not urgent unless it gets loud or you smell exhaust.

gm_ls_v8.s: Check engine light with codes P0327 or P0332. Usually runs fine.
gm_ls_v8.w: The sensors sit under the intake manifold, so it's mostly labor. Replace the sensors and their wiring harness together.

gm_ls_v8.t: Oil pressure sensor leak or bad reading
gm_ls_v8.s: Oil gauge drops to zero or jumps around, or oil leaks at the back of the engine.
gm_ls_v8.w: Check the oil level first. If it's full, the sensor (behind the intake) is usually the problem, not the engine.

gm_afm.t: Active Fuel Management lifter failure (V8 cylinder shutoff)
gm_afm.s: Ticking that gets louder, misfire codes, rough running, a check engine light.
gm_afm.w: Get it checked soon. A collapsed lifter can damage the camshaft. Many owners add an AFM disabler after the repair.

gm_afm.s: Needing to add a quart of oil between changes, fouled spark plugs.
gm_afm.w: Check the oil every fill-up. Shops can replace the PCV/oil deflector parts or piston rings in bad cases.

gm_truck_9907.t: Instrument cluster gauges stick or die
gm_truck_9907.s: Speedometer, fuel or temp needles stick, jump, or drop to zero.
gm_truck_9907.w: The gauge motors on the circuit board wear out. A cluster repair service fixes it for much less than a new cluster.

gm_truck_9907.s: Long crank before starting, sputtering under load, or cranks but won't start.
gm_truck_9907.w: Test fuel pressure (about 55 to 62 psi). The pump is in the tank, so replace the fuel filter and pump together.

gm_truck_9907.s: Soft or sinking brake pedal, brake fluid on the frame rail or above the gas tank.
gm_truck_9907.w: Don't drive it. Brake lines rust through on these trucks; replace the whole line, not just the leak.

gm_truck_9907.s: Loose, wandering steering, a clunk when turning the wheel parked.
gm_truck_9907.w: Cheap parts. Replace them and get an alignment. Lifted trucks and big tires wear them faster.

gm_truck_9907.s: Clicking behind the dash, or air only hot or only cold on one side.
gm_truck_9907.w: The small blend door motor behind the dash fails. It's an inexpensive part.

gm_4l60e.s: Slips or loses 3rd/4th gear, flares between shifts, late or harsh shifts.
gm_4l60e.w: Check the fluid first. A worn 3-4 clutch pack is common; a rebuild is usually the fix.

gm_truck_0714.s: A clunk or knock felt in the steering wheel when turning slowly or parked.
gm_truck_0714.w: The intermediate steering shaft needs grease or replacement. A common, cheap fix.

gm_truck_0714.s: A/C blows warm, then cold after a recharge, then warm again.
gm_truck_0714.w: The condenser up front is easily punctured. Have the leak found before paying for another recharge.

gm_truck_0714.s: Soft brake pedal, fluid near the rear axle or along the frame.
gm_truck_0714.w: Don't drive it. Replace the line and check the others.

gm_truck_0714.s: A shake like driving over rumble strips at 30 to 50 mph.
gm_truck_0714.w: A fluid exchange with the updated fluid often fixes it; if not, the torque converter is replaced.

gm_truck_1418.s: Shudder like rumble strips, clunky or jerky shifts at low speed.
gm_truck_1418.w: GM released a fluid change fix (2015 to 2019). Ask a dealer to check for updates on your VIN.

gm_truck_1418.s: A/C stops blowing cold, often within a few years.
gm_truck_1418.w: The condenser is easily damaged. Find the leak before recharging.

gm_truck_19up.t: Lifter failure on 5.3L and 6.2L V8 (cylinder shutoff)
gm_truck_19up.s: Ticking, misfire codes, rough running, check engine light.
gm_truck_19up.w: Get it in soon; a failed lifter can wreck the camshaft. Check for recalls and warranty coverage.

gm_truck_19up.s: Knocking from the engine, low oil pressure, or the engine shutting off.
gm_truck_19up.w: Check your VIN for the 6.2L (L87) recall at nhtsa.gov/recalls or a dealer. Stop driving if it knocks.

gm_truck_19up.s: Clunky or jerky shifts, especially at low speed.
gm_truck_19up.w: Ask a dealer about software updates and a transmission 'relearn'.

gm_duramax_lb7.s: White or black smoke, rough running, fuel in the oil (oil level rising).
gm_duramax_lb7.w: Injectors were covered by a long warranty; now they're replaced as a set. Don't ignore fuel in the oil.

gm_duramax_cp4.t: CP4 fuel pump failure (LML Duramax, 2011 to 2016)
gm_duramax_cp4.s: Sudden stall or no start, metal shavings in the fuel system.
gm_duramax_cp4.w: Expensive when it fails. Use clean, quality diesel and change fuel filters on time; some owners install a pump protection kit.

gm_trailblazer.s: Running hot at idle or in traffic, a loud roaring fan.
gm_trailblazer.w: The engine fan clutch locks up or slips. A common, moderate repair.

gm_trailblazer.t: Instrument cluster and fuel gauge problems
gm_trailblazer.s: Gauges stick or read wrong; fuel gauge shows empty with gas in the tank.
gm_trailblazer.w: Gauge motors and the fuel level sensor (in the tank) are common failures.

gm_trailblazer.s: Clicking behind the dash, air won't switch vents or temperature.
gm_trailblazer.w: The small door motors behind the dash fail. Inexpensive part.

gm_34_38_v6.t: Intake manifold gasket coolant leak (3.1/3.4/3.8L V6)
gm_34_38_v6.s: Losing coolant with no puddle, sweet smell, overheating, milky oil in bad cases.
gm_34_38_v6.w: Fix it early. Left alone, coolant mixes with oil and ruins the engine bearings.

gm_24_ecotec.s: Oil runs low between changes; oil light comes on.
gm_24_ecotec.w: GM extended the warranty on many. Check oil every fill-up; piston rings are the fix.

gm_24_ecotec.s: Rattle at startup, codes P0008 or P0016.
gm_24_ecotec.w: Usually caused by low oil. Replace the chain, guides and tensioner, and keep the oil full.

gm_36_v6.t: Timing chain stretch (3.0/3.6L V6, about 2007 to 2012)
gm_36_v6.s: Check engine light with P0008/P0017/P0018, rattle at startup, rough running.
gm_36_v6.w: A big job (engine partly apart). Changing oil on time is the best prevention.

gm_lambda.s: Loses 3rd, 5th and reverse gears, or goes into limp mode.
gm_lambda.w: A known failure on 2007 to 2013 models. A transmission shop replaces the 3-5-R wave plate.

gm_lambda.t: Power steering pump or line leaks
gm_lambda.s: Whining when turning, low power steering fluid.
gm_lambda.w: Fix leaks early so the pump doesn't run dry.

gm_cobalt.s: Engine shuts off while driving, power steering and airbags can turn off.
gm_cobalt.w: Serious recall. Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls. Keep only the key on the ring until fixed.

gm_cobalt.s: Steering suddenly gets heavy, power steering warning light.
gm_cobalt.w: The steering motor was recalled on many. Check for open recalls.

gm_14t.s: Coolant smell, low coolant warnings, overheating.
gm_14t.w: The water pump, thermostat housing and coolant hoses often leak. Fix them before the engine overheats.

gm_14t.s: Whistling or squealing at idle, oil leaks, lean codes.
gm_14t.w: The PCV system is built into the valve cover, which gets replaced as one part.

gm_northstar.w: An expensive repair because of how the head bolts are built. Get a second opinion on the cost.

gm_northstar.s: Oil spots under the car, burning oil smell.
gm_northstar.w: The lower engine seals leak with age; a big labor job.

gm_passlock.s: Cranks but won't start, or won't crank, security light flashing.
gm_passlock.w: The anti-theft system misreads the key. A shop can do a 10-minute relearn or replace the ignition sensor.

gm_colorado_0412.s: Misfire on one cylinder, rough running, low compression.
gm_colorado_0412.w: A compression test confirms it. The cylinder head needs a valve job.

gm_colorado_15up.s: Shudder or harsh shifts at low speed.
gm_colorado_15up.w: Ask a dealer about the transmission fluid update.

gm_malibu_0412.s: Clicking or clunk in the steering wheel when turning.
gm_malibu_0412.w: The intermediate steering shaft is replaced. Common and covered on some models.

gm_malibu_0412.s: Steering suddenly gets very heavy, warning light on the dash.
gm_malibu_0412.w: The electric power steering motor fails; check for recalls on your VIN.

gm_equinox_0509.w: Replace the intake gaskets before coolant reaches the oil.

gm_vue_cvt.s: Slipping, whining, or the vehicle won't move.
gm_vue_cvt.w: These CVTs often fail; repair cost can be more than the vehicle is worth. Get a quote first.

gm_inline5.s: Misfire on one cylinder, rough running.
gm_inline5.w: A compression test confirms it; the head needs a valve job.

ford_triton_2v.s: A loud pop, then a ticking/puffing sound and a misfire.
ford_triton_2v.w: The plug threads strip out of the head. A shop installs a thread insert; it's a known fix.

ford_triton_2v.s: Coolant leak at the front of the engine, overheating.
ford_triton_2v.w: The coolant crossover in the plastic intake cracks. Replace it with the updated aluminum-crossover part.

ford_triton_3v.s: Ticking or rattle at idle and at startup, codes P0012/P0021 or P0016.
ford_triton_3v.w: Use the right oil and change it on time. Repair means phasers, chains and guides; a big job.

ford_triton_3v.s: Misfires that need new plugs; shops quote extra time.
ford_triton_3v.w: Have a shop that knows these engines change the plugs with the special tool.

ford_triton_3v.s: Ticking from the engine, louder when cold.
ford_triton_3v.w: Studs break at the back of the manifold. Fix before the gasket burns out.

ford_f150_9703.s: Slipping, delayed shifts, flaring between gears.
ford_f150_9703.w: Check fluid; overdrive and 3-4 clutch wear is common.

ford_f150_0414.s: Stalls or won't start, especially after rain; fuel pump code.
ford_f150_0414.w: The module on the frame rusts. It's an inexpensive part with an updated mounting bracket.

ford_f150_0414.s: Clicking or tapping behind the dash.
ford_f150_0414.w: The blend door actuator fails; inexpensive part.

ford_ecoboost_35.t: Timing chain stretch / cam phaser rattle (3.5L EcoBoost)
ford_ecoboost_35.s: Rattle for a few seconds at cold start, codes P0016 to P0019.
ford_ecoboost_35.w: Ford updated the parts. Fix it before the chain jumps. Change oil on time.

ford_ecoboost_35.s: Stumbles or misfires when you accelerate hard in humid weather.
ford_ecoboost_35.w: Ford released an updated deflector or intercooler. Ask a dealer.

ford_iwe.s: Grinding or clicking from the front wheels while driving in 2WD.
ford_iwe.w: A vacuum leak lets the front hubs partly engage. Fixing the vacuum line or check valve usually solves it.

ford_10r80.s: Clunky, harsh or delayed shifts, especially 1st to 3rd.
ford_10r80.w: Ask the dealer about software updates and an adaptive relearn.

ford_50_coyote.w: Check oil every fill-up and keep records; Ford has covered some under warranty.

ford_27_ecoboost.w: The oil pan was updated; replace it and the gasket.

ford_60_powerstroke.t: 6.0L Power Stroke head gaskets and EGR cooler
ford_60_powerstroke.s: White smoke, losing coolant, coolant pushing out of the tank, overheating.
ford_60_powerstroke.w: A known weak spot (2003 to 2007). 'Bulletproofing' with head studs and new coolers is the long-term fix.

ford_60_powerstroke.s: Engine runs hot, EGR cooler fails repeatedly.
ford_60_powerstroke.w: A shop compares oil and coolant temperatures to diagnose it. Use the right coolant and keep it clean.

ford_64_powerstroke.w: Radiator leaks are very common; check the EGR cooler at the same time.

ford_67_powerstroke.s: Sudden stall or no start; metal in the fuel system.
ford_67_powerstroke.w: Use clean diesel and change fuel filters on time.

ford_death_wobble.s: Violent shaking of the steering wheel after hitting a bump, usually at 45 to 60 mph.
ford_death_wobble.w: Slow down firmly to stop it. Worn track bar, steering damper, ball joints or tie rods; a front-end inspection finds it.

ford_40_sohc.s: Rattle at startup or around 2,000 to 3,000 rpm, check engine light.
ford_40_sohc.w: The timing chain guides and tensioners wear. Fix before it gets louder.

ford_5r55.s: Harsh shifts, slipping, no 2nd gear, or stuck in gear.
ford_5r55.w: The servo bore wears out. A transmission shop can install a fix kit.

ford_35_v6_wp.s: Coolant loss, sweet smell, overheating, milky oil in bad cases.
ford_35_v6_wp.w: The pump is inside the engine, so a leak can mix coolant into the oil. Fix it at the first sign.

ford_35_v6_wp.s: Burning gear-oil smell, leaks near the transmission.
ford_35_v6_wp.w: The power transfer unit overheats its fluid. Change the fluid and fix leaks early.

ford_explorer_1119.s: Exhaust smell inside, especially when accelerating with the A/C on.
ford_explorer_1119.w: Ford released fixes (sealing the rear body). Check for recalls and service bulletins.

ford_ecoboost_small.s: Overheating, low coolant warning, white smoke, misfires.
ford_ecoboost_small.w: Stop driving if it overheats. Ford extended coverage on many; check with a dealer.

ford_powershift.s: Shudder or jerking from a stop, hesitation, slipping, rattling.
ford_powershift.w: Ford extended the clutch warranty on many. A dealer can update software and replace the clutches.

ford_fusion_epas.s: Steering gets heavy suddenly, power steering warning message.
ford_fusion_epas.w: The electric steering was recalled on some years; check your VIN.

ford_cd4e.w: Common on early Escapes; a transmission shop can rebuild it.

ford_panther.s: Coolant leak at the front of the engine, overheating.
ford_panther.w: Replace it with the updated part with the aluminum coolant crossover.

ford_panther.s: Clicking behind the dash, heat stuck on one setting.
ford_panther.w: The blend door actuator fails; inexpensive.

ford_air_susp.s: Sits low on one corner or in the back after parking, suspension warning.
ford_air_susp.w: Air springs and the compressor wear out. Some owners convert to regular coil springs.

ford_mt82.s: Hard shifting or grinding into gears, especially when hot.
ford_mt82.w: Some fixes come from fluid changes and shifter bushings; check for updates.

fca_hemi_tick.t: Hemi lifter and camshaft failure ('Hemi tick')
fca_hemi_tick.s: Ticking that gets worse, misfire codes, rough idle.
fca_hemi_tick.w: Get it checked early. A failed lifter roller damages the camshaft. Change oil on time.

fca_hemi_manifold.s: Ticking when cold that fades as it warms up.
fca_hemi_manifold.w: Replace the broken bolts and gasket; a common repair.

fca_tipm.s: Random no-starts, fuel pump not running, horn or wipers acting on their own.
fca_tipm.w: The power module under the hood fails. Some were recalled; a rebuilt unit is cheaper than new.

fca_pentastar.t: Oil filter housing / oil cooler leak (3.6L V6)
fca_pentastar.s: Oil leak on top of the engine in the back, burning oil smell.
fca_pentastar.w: The plastic housing cracks. Replace it with the updated (often aluminum) part.

fca_pentastar.s: Ticking from the top of the engine, misfire codes.
fca_pentastar.w: Rocker arms and lifters are replaced; the left cylinder head was a known problem on early engines.

fca_47_v8.s: Running hot, losing coolant, white smoke.
fca_47_v8.w: Keep the cooling system healthy; these engines don't tolerate overheating.
Change oil on time. Sludge comes from long oil intervals.

fca_27_v6.t: 2.7L V6 oil sludge and internal water pump
fca_27_v6.s: Losing coolant, overheating, engine knocking or failure.
fca_27_v6.w: Change oil often. The water pump is inside the engine; if it leaks, fix immediately.

fca_ram_lx_susp.s: Clunk over bumps and when braking, uneven tire wear.
fca_ram_lx_susp.w: Front control arms and tension struts wear out. Replace them and get an alignment.

fca_death_wobble.s: Violent steering shake after a bump at highway speed.
fca_death_wobble.w: Slow down firmly to stop it. Worn track bar, tie rods, ball joints or steering damper. A lift makes it more likely.

fca_cummins_emissions.s: Loss of power, more regens, 'exhaust system service' message.
fca_cummins_emissions.w: Highway driving helps the filter clean itself. A shop can clean or replace the EGR and DPF.

jeep_40_rms.s: Oil drips where the engine meets the transmission.
jeep_40_rms.w: Very common and usually slow. Check the level; fix during a clutch or transmission job.

jeep_37_v6.t: 3.7L V6 overheating and dropped valve seats
jeep_37_v6.w: Keep the cooling system healthy; a misfire after overheating needs a compression test.

fca_9speed.s: Harsh, delayed or jerky shifts, hesitation from a stop.
fca_9speed.w: Software updates fixed many. Ask a dealer to check your VIN.

fca_24_tigershark.w: Check the oil every fill-up. Some were covered by a warranty extension.

fca_cvt.s: Whining, slipping, shuddering, or loss of power.
fca_cvt.w: Change CVT fluid more often than the manual says. Check for warranty extensions.

fca_41te.s: Harsh or slipping shifts, stuck in 2nd (limp mode).
fca_41te.w: Check the fluid (it's a special type) and codes. A rebuild is common at high miles.

fca_neon.w: Fix before overheating warps the head.

fca_wk2.t: TIPM fuel pump relay no-start (2011 to 2013)
fca_wk2.s: Cranks but won't start, or stalls.
fca_wk2.w: There was a recall. A dealer can install the external fuel pump relay fix.

fca_wk2.s: Sits low, warning lights, compressor runs a lot.
fca_wk2.w: Air springs and the compressor wear out. Check for leaks.

toyota_frame_rust.s: Rust holes or flaking on the frame, especially near the rear.
toyota_frame_rust.w: Have the frame inspected yearly, especially in salty areas. Check your VIN for recalls and frame replacement.

toyota_sai.s: Check engine light and limp mode after a cold start (P2440 to P2445).
toyota_sai.w: The air pump or valves fail, often from water. Covered by a warranty extension on many trucks.

toyota_57_v8.t: Cam tower / timing cover oil leaks (5.7L)
toyota_57_v8.s: Oil seeping at the back or front of the engine.
toyota_57_v8.w: Usually slow. Watch the oil level; fix at a bigger repair.

toyota_57_v8.s: Coolant smell, pink crust at the front of the engine, low coolant.
toyota_57_v8.w: Replace the water pump before it fails completely.

toyota_2az.w: Toyota extended coverage on many. Check oil every fill-up; piston rings are the fix.

toyota_1zz.s: Oil level drops; blue smoke at startup.
toyota_1zz.w: Check oil often. Piston ring wear is the cause.

toyota_2gr_hose.t: Oil cooler line rubber hose leak (3.5L V6)
toyota_2gr_hose.s: Sudden oil leak at the front of the engine.
toyota_2gr_hose.w: Toyota replaced the rubber section with an all-metal line. Check that yours was updated.

toyota_1mz_sludge.w: Change oil often with good oil. Sludge damage is often found at an oil change.

toyota_dash.s: Dash surface gets sticky, shiny, or glare on the windshield.
toyota_dash.w: Lexus had a warranty program for some years; check with a dealer.

toyota_tacoma_16up.s: Shifts back and forth on hills, feels like it can't pick a gear.
toyota_tacoma_16up.w: Toyota released software updates; ask a dealer.

toyota_tacoma_16up.s: Gear oil on the rear axle or inside the rear wheels.
toyota_tacoma_16up.w: Fix before the differential runs low on oil.

toyota_tundra_22up.t: Engine recall (3.4L twin turbo V6, 2022 to 2023)
toyota_tundra_22up.s: Knocking, loss of power, or engine failure.
toyota_tundra_22up.w: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls; Toyota replaces affected engines.

toyota_prius_3.t: Head gasket / EGR cooler failure (2010 to 2015)
toyota_prius_3.s: Overheating, coolant loss, misfire, knocking at startup.
toyota_prius_3.w: Clean the EGR system at about 100k miles to help prevent it. Fix at the first sign of coolant loss.

toyota_hybrid_battery.s: Worse gas mileage, battery gauge swings fast, warning light.
toyota_hybrid_battery.w: A hybrid shop can test it; rebuilt batteries cost much less than new.

toyota_corolla_0913.s: Coolant smell, pink crust near the pump, low coolant.
toyota_corolla_0913.w: Replace the water pump before it fails.

toyota_rav4_19up.s: Pump clicks off early; range is lower than it should be.
toyota_rav4_19up.w: A known tank design issue on some years; ask a dealer about updates.

lexus_carbon.w: A shop can clean the intake valves (walnut blasting).

honda_trans_9905.s: Slipping, flaring between 2nd and 3rd, transmission light flashing.
honda_trans_9905.w: A well-known weak spot on early 2000s Honda and Acura V6 models. Change fluid with genuine Honda fluid.

honda_vcm.t: VCM (cylinder shutoff) misfires and oil burning
honda_vcm.s: Misfires, fouled spark plugs, shaking at low speed, oil use.
honda_vcm.w: Honda extended coverage on many. Some owners use a VCM disabler after repairs.

honda_vcm.s: Vibration at idle or when the engine switches modes.
honda_vcm.w: The active engine mounts wear out; replace them.

honda_timing_belt.s: No symptom until it breaks, and then the engine stops and can be damaged.
honda_timing_belt.w: Replace the timing belt and water pump about every 100k miles or 7 years.

honda_ac_compressor.s: A/C blows warm, grinding or rattling from the compressor.
honda_ac_compressor.w: When it fails it can spread metal through the A/C system, so the whole system gets flushed.

honda_ac_condenser.w: Honda extended coverage on some; check with a dealer.

honda_vtc_rattle.t: VTC actuator rattle at cold start (2.4L)
honda_vtc_rattle.s: A loud grinding rattle for a second or two at cold start.
honda_vtc_rattle.w: The cam timing (VTC) gear is replaced. Not urgent, but don't wait forever.

honda_civic_0609.s: Coolant leak at the back of the engine, overheating.
honda_civic_0609.w: Honda extended the warranty on many. Check with a dealer.

honda_15t_dilution.s: Oil smells like gas, oil level rising, especially in cold weather.
honda_15t_dilution.w: Honda released software updates and extended coverage in cold states. Change oil on time.

honda_cvt_judder.s: A shudder or vibration when accelerating gently.
honda_cvt_judder.w: Software updates and CVT fluid changes usually fix it.

honda_9speed.w: Software updates help; ask a dealer.

nissan_cvt.s: Whining, shuddering, slipping, loss of power, or limp mode.
nissan_cvt.w: Nissan extended CVT warranties on many. Change CVT fluid about every 30k to 60k miles.

nissan_qr25_precat.s: Rattle under the car, loss of power, oil burning, check engine light.
nissan_qr25_precat.w: Broken pieces can get sucked into the engine. Have it checked if it rattles.

nissan_qr25_precat.s: Stalls while driving or won't restart.
nissan_qr25_precat.w: There was a recall; check your VIN.

nissan_smod.t: Radiator leaks coolant into the transmission ('strawberry milkshake')
nissan_smod.s: Shuddering, slipping, pink milky transmission fluid.
nissan_smod.w: Bypass the radiator's transmission cooler with an external cooler before it happens. Once mixed, the transmission is usually ruined.

nissan_vk56.s: Ticking, especially when cold; exhaust smell.
Gear oil inside the rear wheels, brakes contaminated.
nissan_vk56.w: Replace the axle seals and clean or replace the brake parts.

nissan_ps_hose.s: Whining when turning, fluid on the ground.

nissan_frontier_chain.s: Whining that rises with RPM, codes P0335/P0340.
nissan_frontier_chain.w: Replace the timing chain guides early to avoid engine damage.

infiniti_vq_oil.s: Oil level drops, especially if driven hard.

hk_theta2.s: Knocking that gets louder with RPM, oil light, stalling, oil burning.
hk_theta2.w: Stop driving if it knocks. Hyundai/Kia recalled many and extended warranties; check your VIN.

hk_nu_gamma.s: Knocking, oil burning, loss of power.
hk_nu_gamma.w: Check your VIN for recalls and warranty extensions. Keep oil full.

hk_steering_coupler.s: Clicking or knocking in the steering wheel when turning.
hk_steering_coupler.w: The rubber coupler in the electric steering wears out; an inexpensive part.

hk_theft.t: Easy to steal (key-start models, no immobilizer)
hk_theft.w: Get the free anti-theft software update at a dealer and use a steering wheel lock.

hk_soul_cat.t: Catalytic converter overheating damages pistons (1.6L, recall)
hk_soul_cat.s: Knocking, loss of power, check engine light.
hk_soul_cat.w: There was a recall with software and a warranty extension; check your VIN.

subaru_ej25.s: Oil or coolant seeping at the sides of the engine, overheating, sweet smell.
subaru_ej25.w: One of the most common Subaru repairs. Replace with updated multi-layer gaskets.

subaru_ej25.s: Humming that gets louder with speed.
subaru_ej25.w: Wheel bearings wear on these; replace the noisy one.

subaru_fb_oil.w: Subaru extended coverage on many. Check oil every fill-up.

subaru_cvt.w: Subaru extended CVT warranties on many; ask a dealer about updates.

subaru_battery_drain.s: Dead battery after sitting a day or two.
subaru_battery_drain.w: A known issue; a dealer can check for updates and test for parasitic draw.

vw_mk4_coils.s: Misfires, flashing check engine light, shaking.
vw_mk4_coils.w: Replace the bad coil (and check plugs). Many were recalled.

vw_mk4_coils.s: Oil light, turbo noise, burning oil.
vw_mk4_coils.w: Use the right synthetic oil and change it on time.

vw_ea888_gen1.t: Timing chain tensioner failure (2.0T, about 2008 to 2012)
vw_ea888_gen1.s: Rattle at startup; if it fails, the engine stops and is badly damaged.
vw_ea888_gen1.w: Replace the tensioner with the updated part as prevention. This one is worth doing before it fails.
Piston ring and PCV updates fix it; check oil often.

vw_water_pump.t: Plastic water pump / thermostat housing leaks
vw_water_pump.s: Coolant smell, low coolant warning, pink crust at the pump.
vw_water_pump.w: Replace the pump housing; very common on 2.0T and 1.8T engines.

vw_carbon.t: Carbon buildup on intake valves (direct injection)
vw_carbon.w: Intake valve cleaning (walnut blasting) fixes it.

vw_dsg.s: Jerky low-speed shifts, flashing gear display, clunks.
vw_dsg.w: Change DSG fluid every 40k miles. The mechatronic unit is a common repair.

vw_tdi_hpfp.s: Stalls or won't start; metal in the fuel system.
vw_tdi_hpfp.w: Expensive when it fails. Use clean diesel; never put gas in it.

bmw_cooling.s: Coolant leaks, overheating warning, sweet smell.
bmw_cooling.w: Radiators, expansion tanks, and water pumps fail around 60k to 100k miles. Replace them as a set.

bmw_cooling.t: Oil filter housing and valve cover gasket leaks
bmw_cooling.s: Burning oil smell, oil on the engine.
bmw_cooling.w: Very common. Fix early; oil can ruin the drive belt and cause it to get sucked in.

bmw_n54.t: High-pressure fuel pump failure (N54 twin turbo)
bmw_n54.w: There was an extended warranty; check with a dealer.

bmw_n20.w: Replace the chain and guides before it fails. BMW extended coverage on some.

mini_n14.w: Replace the chain and tensioner before it jumps a tooth.
Check oil often; clean the intake valves.

mini_r50.w: These CVTs often fail; a manual transmission was much more reliable.
The pump's cooling fan fails first; replacing it early can save the pump.

mb_m272.t: Balance shaft / timing gear wear (V6, about 2005 to 2008)
mb_m272.w: A big engine repair. Check service history before buying.

mb_airmatic.s: Sits low after parking, suspension warning.
mb_airmatic.w: Air struts and the compressor wear out.

mb_trans_plate.s: Stuck in one gear (limp mode), harsh shifts.
mb_trans_plate.w: The electronic plate inside the transmission is replaced.

mb_sbc.t: SBC brake system failure (2003 to 2006 E-Class)
mb_sbc.s: Brake warning messages, reduced braking power.
mb_sbc.w: Recalled and covered by extended warranty; check with a dealer.

mazda_cx7.t: Turbo and timing chain problems (2.3L turbo)
mazda_cx7.s: Loss of power, smoke, rattle at startup.
mazda_cx7.w: Change oil often; these turbos and VVT parts need clean oil.

mazda_cx9_wp.s: Losing coolant, overheating, coolant in the oil.
mazda_cx9_wp.w: The pump is inside the engine; fix at the first sign of coolant loss.

mazda_rx8.s: Hard starts, rough idle, low compression, oil burning by design.
mazda_rx8.w: A rotary-specific compression test tells you engine health. Let it warm up before shutting off.

mazda3_0409.s: Bubbling paint and rust around the rear wheels.

volvo_pcv.s: Oil leaks, whistling from the engine, oil burning.
volvo_pcv.w: Replace the PCV oil trap and hoses; common on older Volvos.

volvo_xc90_trans.w: A known weak transmission on early T6 models.

volvo_angle_gear.s: AWD warning, clunk or grinding from the front.
volvo_angle_gear.w: Change its oil; it's often ignored.

tesla_12v.s: Car won't wake up or warnings to replace the 12V battery.
tesla_12v.w: The small 12V battery fails every few years; it's a quick replacement.

tesla_susp.w: Front control arms wear; Tesla service can inspect.

tesla_heatpump.t: Heat pump / A/C failures in cold weather
tesla_heatpump.s: No heat or A/C, warning to service the climate system.
tesla_heatpump.w: Software updates and parts replacements fixed many; check with Tesla service.

lr_air.s: Sits low, suspension fault warning, compressor runs a lot.
lr_air.w: Air springs and the compressor wear out; a common repair on these.

lr_50_chain.w: Replace the chains and guides before they fail.

pt_cruiser.s: Clunk when accelerating or shifting, vibration.
